biography: Nicki Thiim, a name whispered with a mix of respect and frustration in the paddock, hails from the windswept plains of Denmark. He wasn't born into racing royalty; his father ran a small karting track on the outskirts of Viborg, and Nicki spent his formative years tearing around it, often cannibalizing old engines for parts. His raw talent became undeniably apparent at age 16, when he won the Danish Karting Championship three years in a row, a feat that caught the eye of a small Formula Ford team. Despite initial struggles adapting to single-seaters, Thiim's tenacity shone through. His transition to GT racing was almost accidental; a last-minute call-up to replace an injured driver at an AMR-affiliated team turned into a full-time gig. Now at 23, and with a few years under his belt, Thiim is considered a solid midfield driver, often showing flashes of brilliance but struggling with consistency. He is fighting hard to prove he is worthy of a factory seat.
drivingStyle: Thiim is a fiercely defensive driver, a trait that has earned him both admiration and criticism. He's known for his late braking and aggressive positioning, making it incredibly difficult for opponents to overtake him. Tire management isn't his strongest suit; he tends to push too hard early in a stint, often sacrificing pace later in the race. Under pressure, Thiim can become erratic, prone to mistakes that cost him valuable points. He thrives in wet conditions, where his raw car control and willingness to take risks often give him an edge.

rivalries.reason: Rossi accuses Thiim of overly aggressive defending, leading to several on-track collisions and heated exchanges in the media.
Dubois, a seasoned veteran, publicly criticized Thiim's tire management, calling him 'a danger to himself and others' during long stints.
Nakamura, a rising star, has consistently outperformed Thiim despite driving less competitive machinery, fueling Thiim's frustration and envy.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, regardless of the weather.
Before each race, he listens to a specific Danish folk song that his grandfather used to sing.
He refuses to eat anything red on race days, believing it brings bad luck.
famousQuote: "Second is just the first loser. If you're not willing to risk it all, you don't belong on the track."
careerHighlight: Securing a surprise podium finish at the 24 Hours of Spa in 2022, after starting from the back of the grid due to a pre-race mechanical issue, showcasing his resilience and adaptability.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the final corner of the Nürburgring 24 Hours in 2023, costing his team a likely victory and earning him considerable criticism from team management.
